statement: For every 99-by-99 symmetric binary matrix A with zero diagonal and exactly 14 ones in every row, A^2 = 12I - A + 2J over the integers if and only if A^2 = -A + 2J over GF(3). Both equations refer to every matrix entry. I and J have order 99.
source_commit_role: Recorded source context for the written review; separately pinned new working documents are not inferred to be present in that commit.

scope.description: Complete entrywise ternary/integer equivalence in the unrestricted simple symmetric zero-diagonal degree-14 adjacency domain of order 99. No adjacency-common-neighbor or incidence premise.

assumptions: A has order 99; I and J have the same order.
A is symmetric, binary and zero diagonal.
Each row of A has exactly 14 ones over the integers.
The ternary equation is checked for every matrix entry over GF(3).
independent_path: D=A^2-12I+A-2J has every entry divisible by 3.
Simplicity, symmetry and exact degree imply D_uu=14-12-2=0.
For u!=v, D_uv is an integer at least -2; divisibility by 3 therefore implies D_uv>=0.
D times the all-ones vector equals (196-12+14-198) times that vector, hence is zero.
Every entry of a nonnegative matrix with zero row sums is zero, so D=0.
Conversely reduce the full integer equation modulo 3.
written_falsification_checks: Exact integer degree is needed; degree only modulo 3 does not supply the zero row sums.
Symmetry/binary/zero-diagonal premises are needed for the diagonal and sign bounds; other matrix domains are not asserted.
Incomplete entries, rank or sampled residue checks cannot supply entrywise divisibility.
Floating-point residuals or approximate zero cannot supply exact divisibility.
Modulo 2 permits negative defect -2, so this sign argument cannot be transferred to GF(2).
The saved incidence-only rank98 graph fails the target equation and cannot be a counterexample to this equivalence; the synthetic degree95/98 Gram construction violates exact degree14.
No nonzero binary kernel or rank upper bound follows from this implication.
